## Notes (not produced by the script)

- Group B_openphish_now is empty: every OpenPhish candidate was already in the captured set, on a hosting platform or a shortener, so it was excluded. The earlier live probe (0 of 14 caught) used the first hosts of the current OpenPhish list; this run has no sample of that kind.
- Group B_active_sample is a random sample of Phishing.Database ACTIVE entries that are not in our captured set (older, still-listed phishing). Of the 34 with a known age, 29 are older than a year (the other 145 have no registry age: not found or no RDAP server); old domains are the likely reason it is flagged so rarely.
- Group A is new phishing domains from this job's own feed poll (first seen minutes earlier). Offline numbers for the same domains were computed with the same bundle by `js/bench/tier_c_scores.mjs` on the data captured by that poll.
- Legitimate domains (group C) are Tranco-listed, so they are old and established. 0.8% false alarms says nothing about young legitimate sites.
- "http_429" under RDAP result means the registry rate-limited the function's own lookup: 27 of 287 group A domains and 3 of 179 group B domains. It is a reliability limit of the hosted function, not of the model.
- Single run, one day. Counts are small for some cells (for example 5 domains aged 30-365 days in group B).
